_comment: Provenance for WASM bundles built from the pqctoday-hsm repo and vendored into this hub. When you rebuild a bundle with its hsm build script, update its `hsmCommit`/`builtAt`. Verify drift with `npm run sync:wasm:check` (compares against a sibling ../pqctoday-hsm checkout when present; no-op otherwise). Bundles built from other sources (openssl upstream, pqctoday-tpm) are intentionally omitted.

bundles.name: cacp-kmip
bundles._rebuild20260830: Rebuilt 2026-08-30 from hsm branch feat/kmip-engine-key-attributes @ b69be259e (branched off main @ dea9bfa1, NOT hsm main — re-stamp when that branch merges, same as the 2026-08-18 composite-traditional-hash note on this file). Adds one new wasm export, engine_key_attributes(uid), generalizing the existing engine_certificate_attributes pattern to Private/Public/Secret key object types: find_handle_for_object already dispatches on ObjectType generically, so the new function just passes rec.object_type instead of a hardcoded Certificate and reads back CKA_CLASS, CKA_KEY_TYPE, CKA_LABEL, CKA_UNIQUE_ID, CKA_LOCAL, CKA_SENSITIVE, CKA_EXTRACTABLE, CKA_ALWAYS_SENSITIVE, CKA_NEVER_EXTRACTABLE, and whichever size attribute the object carries (CKA_VALUE_LEN / CKA_MODULUS_BITS / CKA_PARAMETER_SET) — never CKA_VALUE/CKA_SEED, which stay engine-blocked for a sensitive/non-extractable key per PKCS#11 v3.2 §4.9/§4.10 exactly as a real caller would see. Driven by a real gap: the hub's KMIP Developer tab Keystore view could list objects but had no way to inspect a key's real engine-side attributes (only engine_certificate_attributes existed, certificate-only). Output changed: pqctoday_kmip_wasm_bg.wasm 5761765 -> 5766314 bytes, sha256 b68185ab...3ba7e788 (was 8f4de767...6cd33bb6) — 4549 bytes added, consistent with one new exported function. Verified by the build's own smoke suite running IN wasm (engine bootstrap, OASIS Query/Create round trips, malformed-frame path, ML-DSA-65 CreateKeyPair/Sign/SignatureVerify — 3309-byte signature, Valid — Falcon-512 correctly rejected with keystore unchanged at 3, X25519MLKEM768 hybrid KEM CreateKeyPair→Activate→Encapsulate→Decapsulate round trip) — all PASS, and a live browser Playwright check exercising the new hub-side engineKeyAttributes() binding against a real generated key.

Touches kmip/Cargo.toml + kmip/src/ops/helpers.rs — a real functional change to this bundle's engine surface, not inert drift. Output changed: pqctoday_kmip_wasm_bg.wasm 5746344 -> 5758951 bytes, sha256 789a90b5...a0e8a8da (was d66669f8...7b2450eb). Built from the pqctoday-hsm main checkout (verified `git status --short --branch` showed `## main...origin/main` with a clean tree, at exactly dea9bfa1 — not a worktree carrying unmerged branch commits) so the artifact matches what hub CI's sibling clone of hsm origin/main will see. Build's own smoke suite re-ran and passed (engine bootstrap, OASIS Query/Create round trips, malformed-frame path, ML-DSA-65 CreateKeyPair/Sign/SignatureVerify — 3309-byte signature, Valid — Falcon-512 correctly rejected with keystore unchanged at 3, X25519MLKEM768 hybrid KEM CreateKeyPair→Activate→Encapsulate→Decapsulate round trip). 144 corpus tests re-staged (mandatory=95, optional=7, pqc=42).

bundles._rebuild20260818b: Rebuilt 2026-08-18 from hsm main @ 5a107b2 via scripts/build-kmip-wasm.sh, closing a 1-commit drift since e317f0a9: the composite-hybrid certificate-management audit's engine-side follow-up (kmip-certificate-management-remediation-plan-08182026.md) — adds the .46 composite profile (id-MLDSA65-ECDSA-P384-SHA512, the 8th and last one against the draft's full §6 set), documents a known non-canonical-DER validate.rs/spki_verify.rs risk with no behavior change, fixes a stale test comment, and tightens Register/Import to reject non-canonical certificate DER at accept time. bundles._rebuild20260814: Rebuilt 2026-08-14 from hsm main @ 3f64964 via scripts/build-kmip-wasm.sh, closing a 21-commit drift over kmip/wasm since d9b3f42: the PKCS#11 v3.2 audit-remediation stack (fix/pkcs11-v32-audit-remediation-0813, merged via #171) plus refactor/typed-param-reader-0814 (#172) and the follow-up wasm-target fix (#173, e8b4129 — ck_abi is cfg'd out on wasm32 but #172's get_attr_ulong referenced it directly, breaking the wasm32 build; ck_param::WORD reads the same width fact on every target and is what the fix switched to). hsm was fast-forwarded 38affc0..3f64964 first (1 commit, docs-only: CHANGELOG/docs/refs/README/exceptions.json correcting a false claim about the Complete Provider profile — no source under kmip/ or wasm/). Verified by the build's own smoke suite running IN wasm, not by exit code: engine bootstrap, OASIS Query + Create round trips, a malformed-frame path, ML-DSA-65 CreateKeyPair/Sign/SignatureVerify (3309-byte signature, Valid), Falcon-512 correctly rejected with the keystore unchanged, and an X25519MLKEM768 hybrid KEM CreateKeyPair→Activate→Encapsulate→Decapsulate round trip — all PASS. 144 corpus tests re-staged (mandatory=95, optional=7, pqc=42). Staged into BOTH hub worktrees (pqctoday-hub and pqctoday-hub-main) by running build-kmip-wasm.sh twice with HUB= pointed at each.
bundles._buildNote: Rebuilt 2026-08-13 from hsm main @ d9b3f42 via scripts/build-kmip-wasm.sh, after the KMIP 3.0 item-10 stack merged (#166/#167/#168/#169): Baseline Server profile is now 13/13, with all five server-to-client operations implemented, and the OASIS corpus carries machine-checked provenance against the CSD02 zip. The restage also uncovered that the wasm target had not compiled since #166 — server/secp384r1mlkem1024.rs uses rustls without the native-only cfg gate its neighbour listener.rs already carries — fixed in hsm #170. This bundle is built from the tree WITH that fix, which is why the recorded commit is #170's merge rather than #169's — at 8ffdd1f the wasm target does not compile at all, so no artifact can correspond to it. #170 also adds a wasm32 type-check to the local gate so the next such break is caught by the gate rather than by the next person to restage. Verified by the build's own smoke suite running IN wasm, not by exit code: ML-DSA-65 CreateKeyPair/Sign/SignatureVerify round trip (3309-byte signature, Valid), Falcon-512 correctly rejected with the keystore unchanged, and an X25519MLKEM768 hybrid KEM CreateKeyPair→Activate→Encapsulate→Decapsulate round trip. 144 corpus tests staged (mandatory=95, optional=7, pqc=42).
bundles._rebuild20260818: Rebuilt 2026-08-18 from hsm branch fix/composite-traditional-hash @ 2ecc5268 — composite traditional hash corrected to ecdsa-with-SHA256 (P-256) / -SHA384 (P-384) per draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs §6; the SHA512 in the profile name is the pre-hash PH, not the traditional algorithm's hash. Verified interoperable with the Bouncy Castle IETF Hackathon r5 trust anchor in both directions. NOTE: built from a branch, not hsm main — re-stamp when that branch merges.

bundles._rebuild20260814: Rebuilt 2026-08-14 from hsm main @ 3f64964 via rust/build-wasm-bundle.sh, closing a 21-commit drift over rust/ since d9b3f42 (the PKCS#11 v3.2 audit-remediation + typed-param-reader + wasm-target-fix stack, #171/#172/#173 — same range described in cacp-kmip's 2026-08-14 note). This one is a REAL export-surface change, not the false-drift pattern the 2026-08-08/09 notes below warn about: _C_GetMechanismInfo and _C_GetSlotInfo's first parameter is renamed slot_id (was _slot_id) because ck_param-based code now actually reads it, where the old ck_abi-only path left it unused. wasm binary 2916703 -> 2973086 bytes. A build had already been run at hsm 38affc0 (one commit behind the fast-forwarded 3f64964, which is docs-only) and left uncommitted in rust/pkg_bundler/; rerunning build-wasm-bundle.sh at the fast-forwarded HEAD reproduced BYTE-IDENTICAL output (same sha256 for both _bg.wasm and _bg.js), proving the earlier build was already correct rather than trusting that on assertion. Staged into BOTH hub worktrees' public/wasm/rust/ and src/wasm/ (5 files each: softhsmrustv3.js, softhsmrustv3_bg.js, softhsmrustv3_bg.wasm, softhsmrustv3.d.ts, softhsmrustv3_bg.wasm.d.ts) from rust/pkg-release/ — the .d.ts files aren't touched by build-wasm-bundle.sh's own tracked-artifact copy (it only refreshes rust/pkg_bundler/{.js,_bg.js,_bg.wasm}), so they were copied by hand and now carry the renamed parameters too.
bundles._rebuild20260813: Rebuilt 2026-08-13 from hsm main @ d9b3f42 and the output was BYTE-IDENTICAL to the previous bundle (sha256 310d3a911b62e66bd1a1beaefcd641b835183cc7c1377960fbe03112485982a7) — which is precisely why it is worth recording. The sibling openssl-pkcs11 bundle had shipped four days of stale bytes because its build path consumes a prebuilt archive; this one runs cargo directly, so it had already picked up hsm d07dfa9 (RSA private keys expose CKA_MODULUS/CKA_PUBLIC_EXPONENT). Established by rebuilding and comparing digests, NOT by trusting the build timestamp — 'the bundle was built after the fix landed' is exactly the reasoning that proved wrong for openssl-pkcs11. Re-anchor only; no behaviour change.
bundles._buildNote: Re-anchored 2026-08-09 to hsm main @ 1cab535. REBUILT AND PROVEN IDENTICAL rather than re-anchored on assertion: running rust/build-wasm-bundle.sh at 1cab535 produced softhsmrustv3_bg.wasm, softhsmrustv3_bg.js, softhsmrustv3.js and both .d.ts files BYTE-IDENTICAL to the ones already shipped (wasm sha256 310d3a91…), so no file in the hub changed — only this pin. The source diff predicts exactly that: between the previously recorded 3e2f5055b and 1cab535, the only change anywhere under rust/ is rust/bench-harness/src/kmip.rs, which no bundle builds from. Export surface unchanged at 91 distinct C_* symbols (same set), and the binary contains zero bench-harness symbols. NOTE FOR THE NEXT READER: this bundle's sourceDirs is ['rust'], which CONTAINS rust/bench-harness, so the drift gate counts bench commits as inputs and will keep reporting false drift here. Rebuilding on that signal is how bench code would get baked into shipped wasm — check the diff excludes rust/bench-harness before believing a stale report. RE-ANCHORED to dc9c0a838 (same day, minutes later): committing the rebuilt artifact back to hsm is ITSELF a commit under rust/, so the gate immediately reported 1 commit of fresh drift against a bundle that had just been proven current — the tail-chase the 2026-08-08 note on this file already described. dc9c0a838 changes exactly one file, rust/pkg_bundler/softhsmrustv3_bg.wasm, which is the tracked build OUTPUT the hub vendors, not a source input. Verified rather than asserted: the wasm shipped here and the blob inside dc9c0a838 have the same sha256 (310d3a91…), so this pin names the commit that literally CONTAINS the bytes being shipped. This will recur every time an artifact is committed back to hsm while these bundles keep 'rust' in sourceDirs.
bundles._priorBuildNote20260808: Rebuilt 2026-08-08 from hsm main @ 3480bec (v0.21.0) via rust/build-wasm-bundle.sh, closing a 6-commit drift over rust/. No functional change reachable from this target: the v0.21.0 rust/ work is the operation-evidence log, and its sink is cfg-gated OUT on wasm32-unknown-unknown (see the 'WASM targets must keep building' note in rust/src/oplog.rs), which is why no PQCEV string appears in the bundl
bundles._reanchor20260815: Re-anchored 2026-08-14 to hsm 65d3100 without rebuilding: that commit only touches rust/pkg_bundler/ (the build OUTPUT vendored back into hsm itself), 0 changes under rust/src/ (verified: git show --stat shows two pkg_bundler files only) — its own commit message documents the rebuild was byte-identical to the prior one. Committing an artifact back to a sourceDir the gate watches is the exact tail-chase this file's own 2026-08-09 note on softhsmrustv3-engine already described; re-anchoring is the documented fix, not a rebuild.

Only 10 of those 85 touch this bundle's sourceDirs, and only 3 carry real rust/src code: b38cee2 (real Ed448 keygen/sign/verify — crypto/handlers.rs +147, ffi.rs +78, conformance_v32_tests.rs +122, Cargo.lock/toml), ee7f9aa (#187 CACP modular policies + hardening — store/{crypto,memory,mod,sqlite}.rs +782 combined, ffi.rs +213, state.rs +124, native/{hbs,object,session}.rs) and dea9bfa (#188 WS-11 v3.2 conformance gaps — ffi.rs +844, state.rs +83, constants.rs +9, native/mod.rs; a real 68-entry C_GetFunctionList and C_Finalize no longer wiping TOKEN_STORE on library unload/reload). The remaining 7 are inert for this target: 5cc647b is the vendored rust/pkg_bundler wasm blob (a DIFFERENT bundle's build OUTPUT, softhsmrustv3-engine's), and c54ea27/4b9e726/ae664d8/1ba06ab/9211c1e/25ffe21 are each a one-line RUST_P11_V32_CONFORMANCE_REPORT.md timestamp regen. So this is a real functional change, not lockfile-or-report-only drift — and it is proven by artifact, not asserted: the rust staticlib hash MOVED (845891bd...d7708b8 -> 946e6832...a44b473, 6876488 -> 6964830 bytes) while the pkcs11-provider archive rebuilt with FORCE=1 came out BYTE-IDENTICAL (6495f729...b53c4a, unchanged since 2026-08-14), exactly matching the source read that src/vendor/pkcs11-provider and scripts/build-openssl-wasm.sh have ZERO commits in the range (both `git log 94a5797b3..dea9bfa18 -- <dir>` outputs empty). PROVENANCE CORRECTION — the bytes this entry replaces were NOT built at the recorded 94a5797/2026-08-24: public/wasm/openssl-link-inputs.json as committed at HEAD records linked_at 2026-08-28T13:07:11Z against a rust staticlib sha256 b74ea978...ce576d, which is neither 845891bd (what hsm main @ 94a5797 produces, per this bundle's own 2026-08-24b note) nor any archive present anywhere on disk today. That manifest also recorded pkcs11_provider_ar as an ABSOLUTE path into the main hsm checkout while softhsm_ar was stripped relative, which only happens when PKCS11_PROVIDER_AR is overridden and HSM_ROOT points somewhere other than main hsm — the only other emscripten-capable checkout being .worktrees/openssl-provider-remediation on feat/jdk27-jca-provider (aaa9d80, ~20 commits unmerged into main, confirmed NOT an ancestor of dea9bfa18). So the shipped bundle carried unattributable, probably-unmerged branch code while provenance read 'current' — the same class of miss as the 2026-08-13 postmortem below, caught this time by the link manifest that postmortem added. This rebuild replaces it with bytes provably linked from hsm main @ dea9bfa1. Output: openssl.wasm 7006326 -> 7023122 bytes, sha256 e1ba00b2...d6d316 -> 47e77e37...cca4cf6; openssl.js BYTE-IDENTICAL (267457 bytes, sha256 464d1db5...c9a7bdd7) — correct, since LINK_FLAGS and the EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS list did not change. VERIFIED BY ARTIFACT, not exit code: the .wasm parses as a real module (new WebAssembly.Module, 65 exports / 65 imports); the export surface was compared LIKE-FOR-LIKE against the binary being replaced — 65 in both with an EMPTY symmetric difference; pqctoday_cms_init, pqctoday_composite_mkcert, pqctoday_composite_cms_sign, execute_cmp_simulation, generate_mock_ca_root, cmp_main, C_GetFunctionList and C_Initialize are all exported; `openssl version` reports 3.6.3 through the real Node driver. The hub's own KAT suite ran GREEN against THIS binary on Node 24 — 34/34 across src/test/kat/{openssl-driver,anchor,mldsa-cross-impl,mlkem-cross-impl,openssl-kem-decap-flag}.test.ts: Node-produced ML-DSA-44/65/87 and SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s signatures verify under this WASM with bit-flip and wrong-message negatives correctly rejected, ML-KEM-512/768/1024 decap recovers Node's exact shared secret with the FIPS 203 implicit-rejection branch behaving, the pinned anchor fixtures verify, and pkeyutl genpkey->pubout->encap->decap round-trips. openssl-link-inputs.json's two input sha256s match the freshly built archives and its output_sha256 matches the shipped openssl.wasm. CLAIM CORRECTED: the 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-24 notes below both record 'C_EncapsulateKey present in the binary'. It is NOT in the export table, and it is not in build-wasm.sh's EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS list either — and it is absent from the binary this rebuild REPLACES as well, so nothing regressed; those notes were reading an unanchored substring grep (C_DecapsulateKey does appear as a symbol string in both binaries). The ML-KEM path ships via the CLI encap/decap subcommands, which the KAT above exercises for real. BUILD-SCRIPT HAZARD, found here and NOT fixed (pqctoday-priv was read-only for this task): build-wasm.sh computes PATCH_DIR from `dirname "$0"` AFTER it has already `cd "$OPENSSL_SRC"`, so invoking it as a bare `bash build-wasm.sh` from pqctoday-priv resolves PATCH_DIR to <openssl-src>/openssl-wasm-patches, which does not exist — and the `if [[ -d "$PATCH_DIR" ]]` guard then skips the entire patch loop SILENTLY. This run printed no 'applying'/'already applied' line at all. The binary is nonetheless correct: openssl-3.6.3-src is a persistent gitignored tree that already carried 0001-apps_startup-register-pkcs11-provider.patch from an earlier absolute-path invocation, verified directly rather than assumed (apps/openssl.c carries the pqctoday_cms_init() hook, a reverse dry-run of the patch applies cleanly, and the expected 'undefined symbol: pqctoday_cms_init' failure of `make apps/openssl` is itself proof the hook is compiled in). But a rebuild against a FRESH openssl tree invoked this way would silently ship exactly the regression that patch file's own header describes — pkcs11: URIs dead in every CLI command. Invoke with an absolute script path until PATCH_DIR is hoisted above the cd. Two further environment facts for the next reader: openssl-3.6.3-src does NOT exist in the .claude/worktrees/dev-tabs-pkcs11-kmip worktree (it is gitignored and lives only in the main pqctoday-hub checkout), so OPENSSL_SRC had to be set explicitly while HUB_ROOT pointed at the worktree; and the hsm main checkout was clean EXCEPT rust/pkg_bundler/softhsmrustv3_bg.wasm, which is a tracked build OUTPUT of the softhsmrustv3-engine bundle (rust/build-wasm-bundle.sh), not an input to this one.

bundles._rebuild20260813: Rebuilt 2026-08-13 from hsm main @ d9b3f42, and the reason matters more than the rebuild. The 2026-08-09 entry below reasoned that rust/ had 'no real input change — only rust/bench-harness moved', and so relinked openssl.wasm without rebuilding libsofthsmrustv3.a. That reasoning was wrong: hsm d07dfa9 (2026-08-09 17:28) had changed rust/src/ffi.rs to expose CKA_MODULUS and CKA_PUBLIC_EXPONENT on RSA private keys, without which pkcs11-provider's fetch_rsa_key() fails its required fetch, never populates the optional CKA_ID, and reports the misleading 'No CKA_ID in source object'. The bundle was linked at 21:42 that evening — four hours after the fix — from an archive built Aug 8 23:42, the day before it. Both recorded commits (1cab535, dc9c0a838) genuinely contain the fix, so provenance read 'current' the entire time while the shipped bytes did not have it, and e2e/cms-workshop-crypto.spec.ts:392 (LAMPS composite id-MLDSA44-RSA2048-PSS-SHA256) failed nightly from 2026-08-09 to 2026-08-13. Only the RSA profile failed; the ECDSA profiles passed, because an EC or ML-DSA public key is derivable from its private key and the provider never needs to resolve a sibling object. This rebuild deletes both input archives first so a skipped rebuild cannot hide, then rebuilds libsofthsmrustv3.a (cargo rustc --release --target wasm32-unknown-emscripten, confirmed by a 'Compiling softhsmrustv3' line and a changed size) and libpkcs11-provider.a before relinking. build-wasm.sh now also writes public/wasm/openssl-link-inputs.json recording the SHA-256 of every archive it links, because a commit comparison cannot see a stale intermediate and this one went unseen for four days.
